To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of sub-cutaneous low-dose heparin to sequential compression devices for the prophylaxis against thrombo-embolism in patients undergoing surgery for gynaecologic malignancies does no improve the outcome and that adding heparin was associated with increased cost, additional nursing time and patient pain.
the addition of sub-cutaneous low-dose heparin to the use of sequential compression devices in women undergoing surgery does not improve the outcomes.

the addition of sub-cutaneous low-dose heparin to sequential compression devices for prophylaxis for deep venous thrombo-embolism in women undergoing surgery to treat gynecologic malignancy did not improve the outcome and was associated with additional cost, additional nursing time, and additional pain.

the use of thromboembolitic prophylaxis in patients who undergo surgery for gynecological malignancy.

there is no evidence that adding subcutaneous low dose heparin to sequential compression devices improves the outcome in patients undergoing surgery for gynaecological malignancy.
there is no evidence that heparin added to SCDs improves outcome in gynecologic malignancy patients.
SCDs are the preferred thromboembolic method of prophylactic treatment for gynecologic oncologic patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of sub-cutaneous low dose heparin to the sequential compression device does not improve the outcomes in the prevention of thromboembolisms in women undergoing surgery.

the use of subcutaneous unfractionated heprin in addition to SCDs does not improve the prevention of venous thromboemblism in gynecological cancer patients undergoing surgery for suspected gynocological malignancies.

the addition of sub cutaneous low dose unfractionated heeparin to SCD's for prophylaxis of deep venous thrombo-embolism in women undergoing surgery of gynecologic malignancy did not improve the outcome and adding heparin was not only more expensive, but also time consuming and painful.

there are many different types of thromboembolisms that are not all treated the same.
